decisions.text: ADOPT run #7's spec rather than author a new one. Run #7 stress-tested and taste-gated an identical trickle brief, reshaped it from guard-accretion to guard-REDUCTION, then delivered zero work cycles (381/381 spawns dead on HTTP 429). Re-authoring the scope would re-derive a conclusion already reached and paid for; L-045 forbids exactly that. Inherited items are re-verified against the repo before prioritization, which already caught one false premise (see D-R8-2).

Run #7's R-1 named a ">= 121 tests" COUNT floor to retire. Cycle 0 grepped test/ at HEAD and found no such literal floor anywhere. The inherited premise is unconfirmed, so S-1 was re-shaped to MEASURE the inventory of count-claim guards first and retire only what the inventory shows exists. L-045 (re-verify inherited SPEC items) and L-031 (measure before planning against an inferred gap) both applied, and both paid at cycle 0.

Taste judge scored use-twice 4 / product-not-demo 6 / scope-fits-night 7 / one-memorable-thing 6 and caught that S-1/S-4/S-5 could each be discharged by publishing prose. Spec CHANGED at lock rather than annotated: S-6 now requires every published finding to ship as a rerunnable tool in tools/, and S-7 requires the escalation to be written as launch-ready brief text for run #9. The use-twice 4 is recorded and not argued away — it is the honest cost of a fourth consecutive trickle brief on a finished program.

L-038 exhausted-window refusal test RUN, not assumed — this is the check the last two runs failed. Probe at kickoff: weekly_used_pct 6.0 at week_elapsed_pct 4.819, weekly reset 2026-08-31T04:59:59Z (well past stop_at), gear 4, ratio 0.32, probe_ok true. Capacity is real; the run OPENS. Contrast run #7, whose kickoff probe wrote weekly_used_pct 100 fifteen minutes before 381 dead spawns.

PLAN independently reproduced cycle 0's D-R8-2 finding by a different route (.github/workflows/test.yml carries an explicit written refusal to add a count assertion), and raised a SECOND premise objection: S-5's 127-vs-129 gap is most likely CI depth-1 skips vs a local full clone, not staleness — both numbers true of different environments. Neither is accepted as fact; W-1 and W-5 exist to measure them, and both items now carry the counter-hypothesis in their notes so a builder cannot quietly assume the spec's framing.

The entire citation-window risk is concentrated in W-7, the only item touching test/ (inside the README citation pathspec). Closing that window needs a new Actions run id, requiring both a successful push and Actions API access — neither confirmed from this environment. W-7 is sequenced last among code-touching items, gated on a confirmed ability to obtain a run id, and must predict the window in its own commit message (S-8). Every other item lands in tools/, docs/ or REPORT.md, outside the pathspec. L-043's pathspec-guard clause applied at PLAN time rather than discovered at merge time.

W-3 PASSES its acceptance clause and the conductor still recorded a defect against it. The clause scopes failability to perturbing the QUOTE, and that direction attributes correctly. The conductor also perturbed the README side -- a case the clause does not cover -- and the check still printed `docs/node-support-citation-history.md has diverged`, blaming the document that did not move. Every factual clause in that message is true; only the direction of attribution is wrong. Rounding this into a FAIL would discard verified work over a case the clause never asked for; burying it would be the gate opening itself by silence. Recorded as new item P-1 instead, with the exact perturbation that produces it.

P-1 PASSES all three directions of its acceptance clause and the conductor still recorded a defect against it — the same ruling shape as D-R8-7. The tool resolves its third anchor with `git show HEAD:<path>`, and git walks UP the directory tree: from a checkout that is not itself a repo but sits inside one, the anchor silently resolves against the ANCESTOR repo. Measured: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from a nested .git-deleted clone returns /opt/targets/aphorism-cli. In the gate the ancestor was the same project, so the attribution looked right — the coincidence is what makes it worth fixing. Run genuinely outside any repo, the fallback fires correctly and honestly, so the builder`s untested path is now exercised and works. Recorded as new item P-2 rather than rounded into a FAIL, because the clause covers three directions and all three pass.

The conductor`s own W-5 gate script carried a bug: its README row-parser assumed five pipe-separated columns, but the table has two columns with the counts in prose, so it parsed zero rows and printed `depth-1 == README row? -> NO`. That NO was the gate failing, not W-5. Corrected in a second script (gate-c3-w5b.mjs), which parses all four rows and reports YES. Recorded here rather than silently re-run, because a gate that misreports must be as visible as a build that does — the evidence file names the bug explicitly.

The conductor's own W-7 gate carried a parser bug, the SECOND cycle running (cf. D-R8-9). Cell C1 read `git status --porcelain` and called .trim() on stdout BEFORE splitting into lines, which ate the leading space of the first line's two-character status column; the path was then sliced one byte short and C1 reported the modified file as "est/readme-tags.test.js", failing the cell on a file that does not exist. The item was NOT rounded to a FAIL and the cell was NOT quietly re-run: it is corrected in runs/gate-c4-w7-c1-addendum.mjs, which documents the defect in its own header and additionally checks something the original missed — that no .scratch tree survives into the commit. Two gate-parser bugs in two consecutive cycles is now a pattern in the conductor's own instruments, not an isolated slip, and it is the RETRO candidate of this run: gate scripts are written once and run once, so they get none of the scrutiny the code under test gets.

The single citation window S-8 permits was opened and CLOSED inside cycle 4, rather than left open across a cycle boundary. Hard rule 4 (green main before the cycle commits) and S-8 (green every commit bar one predicted window) are in tension — recorded as blocked item P-7 for a human ruling — and this cycle resolved it by satisfying both literally: commit 02f4668 opens the window and NAMES it in advance in its own message, and the next commit closes it, so the cycle ENDS green. The enabling measurement was cheap and was taken before dispatch rather than assumed: `gh run list` returns run ids, master is level with origin/master, and CI end-to-end is ~23 seconds. D-R8-6 had gated W-7 on "a confirmed ability to obtain a run id"; that gate was checked, not waived.

W-8 is unsatisfiable as shipped and would have failed SILENTLY. tools/mutation-matrix.mjs pins BASELINE to 20b7ede, so "re-run the matrix at final HEAD" (W-8's clause) would have measured the baseline twice and produced a guaranteed-identical matrix — which the clause explicitly anticipates as a possible legitimate null result ("if W-7 ends in the keep-both branch this still runs and should show an identical matrix"). The two outcomes are observationally identical, so a builder could have discharged W-8 honestly and been wrong. Caught by reading the tool before dispatching against it, not at W-8's gate. W-12 filed as a hard dependency.

The two gate-parser bugs of cycles 3 and 4 (D-R8-9, D-R8-10) were treated as a standing hazard rather than as closed incidents. The cycle-5 gate was written with the cycle-4 defect named in its own header as a rule: split `git status --porcelain` into lines BEFORE any trim, and take the path as line.slice(3) — trimming whole stdout first is what ate the leading space of the status column last cycle. Cell C1 additionally prints every status line BRACKETED, so a column-eating bug is visible in the evidence itself rather than inferable only from a wrong verdict. Three gate scripts in a row have now carried a defect or a defence against one; the instruments deserve the same scrutiny as the code they judge, and this run should say so in RETRO.

The conductor did NOT re-reproduce W-13's pre-fix crash and does not claim to. The item asked the BUILDER for a pre-fix contrast, and the builder reproduced it with the cycle-4 signature (spawnSync git ENOENT inside resetClone, plus a second, worse mode: two runs silently interleaving on one shared clone without crashing). The conductor verified the pre-fix hazard STRUCTURALLY instead — cell C6 shows the old SCRATCH_ROOT was a process-invariant constant with no pid/random/mkdtemp component, so two concurrent runs necessarily resolved the same path — and verified the POST-fix behaviour by live demonstration (C9: 81s of genuine overlap, two distinct mkdtemp dirs, both exit 0, no ENOENT). Recorded because the distinction matters: "conductor-verified" covers the fix and the old code's shape, while the crash reproduction is builder-reported and cycle-4-observed. Rolling those together would overstate what the gate proved.

The conductor's own gate carried a defect for the THIRD consecutive cycle, and this one was caught by re-running the gate rather than by reading it. Cell C1 hardcoded the expected dirty set as [".swarm/backlog.json", "tools/mutation-matrix.mjs"] — true at verification time, false the instant step 7 wrote .swarm/state.json. The cell's own title says .swarm/ is conductor-owned, so state.json was always meant to be permitted: the list was a point-in-time SNAPSHOT masquerading as a RULE. Re-running the gate after persist therefore reported FAIL on a cell whose subject — the builder's write scope — had not changed at all. Handled exactly as D-R8-9 and D-R8-10 were: not re-labelled, not silently re-run. The C1 verdict of record stays the one taken at verification time (PASS, before persist), and runs/gate-c5-c1-addendum.mjs restates the cell as the rule it should always have been — builder scope is tools/mutation-matrix.mjs, every .swarm/ path is the conductor's — so it is re-runnable at any point in the cycle. The addendum also carries a converse control naming three paths the rule must reject, because a scope check that cannot fail is not evidence. Three cycles, three instrument defects, three DIFFERENT root causes (five-column parse of a two-column table; .trim() eating a status column; a snapshot used as an invariant). The common factor is not any one bug: gate scripts are written once, run once, and reviewed by nobody, while the code they judge gets a builder, a gate and a converse control. This is the run's primary RETRO candidate.

A FOURTH instrument defect, found at step 8 of the same cycle that recorded the third. The dashboard renderer hardcodes one burn-up bar labelled "cycle 0 — 0 verified" (runs/run8-render-dashboard.mjs lines 70-71) and then self-checks it against burnup_bars_expected: 1, so it reports ok:true / 1-of-1 bars while publishing a flat empty progress strip — through five cycles and eleven verified items. The self-check validating the renderer against its own hardcoded intent, rather than against cycle.md step 8, is what let it survive. Filed as KI-36 and deferred rather than patched: the cycle was already committed and journalled, and an unrecorded fix to the reporting instrument is exactly the move this run keeps refusing. Note what this does to the pattern in D-R8-15: it is no longer "gate scripts get no scrutiny" but "one-shot instruments get no scrutiny" — the gates, and now the renderer. The RETRO candidate widens accordingly.

A FIFTH consecutive cycle of conductor-instrument defects, and the first in which ONE gate carried four at once. runs/gate-c6.mjs returned 7/12 and every one of the five failures but none of the dispatched work was at fault. (1) C2 located `if (JSON_OUTPUT)` with a whole-file findIndex and asserted an ordering against it, but that text occurs TWICE and legitimately so - L624 inside the one-line P() stream router and L804 as the stdout emit block; the cell took the first and failed a true subject. (2)+(3) C8 and C9 perturbed README by rewriting the string '### Node support' to '### Node support  ', and tools/citation-rule-check.mjs extracts its section by an EXACT match on '\n### Node support\n' (line 57), so the edit DELETED the heading and the tool exited at line 85 on the no-section branch - taken before any git-anchor attribution runs. Both P-2 cells measured a code path neither was about. (4) C11 parsed TAP-style '# pass N' from `node --test`, whose default reporter emits 'ℹ pass N', so pass and fail both read -1 and the cell failed a suite whose own output, printed three lines above the verdict, reads pass 128 / fail 0. (5) C12 read package.json to prove the dependency surface unchanged; this repo has never had one, and the cell reported the standing invariant violated on an ENOENT. Handled as D-R8-9, D-R8-10 and D-R8-15 were: nothing re-labelled, nothing silently re-run. The original gate is committed AS IT RAN, verdicts and all, and runs/gate-c6-addendum.mjs re-takes the four defective cells with each defect named in its own header. All five corrected cells pass, so the cycle-6 verdict rests on 12 cells. Note what the four root causes have in common with the previous three: nothing. Five-column parse of a two-column table; .trim() eating a status column; a snapshot used as an invariant; a renderer self-checked against its own hardcoded intent; and now a first-match regex, a perturbation that never reached its subject, a wrong reporter format, and a file assumed into existence. Eight distinct root causes across five cycles. The constant is not any bug class - it is that one-shot instruments are written once, run once, and reviewed by nobody, while the code they judge gets a builder, a gate, and a converse control. Two of the four defects here were caught ONLY because the raw evidence was printed next to the verdict and visibly contradicted it; that habit, not care, is what is doing the work. This is the run's primary RETRO candidate and it is now supported by eight instances rather than three.

The suite is 128 tests at HEAD against a run baseline of 129, and that DROP is recorded as a pass rather than explained away. It is W-7 (cycle 4) consolidating the two guards that read the same 'Tags on exactly one entry' row, which is what closed KI-R6-3, and must-have S-1 states outright that a test-count drop is a PASS. The attribution is not taken on the conductor's say-so: the C4 identity control measured both revisions on untouched scratch clones and reports baseline 20b7ede at 129 tests / 129 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped GREEN and HEAD e40736c at 128 / 128 / 0 / 0 GREEN, so the -1 is located at a specific commit by an instrument that had no stake in the answer.

KI-36 is CLOSED rather than carried, and the reasoning for reversing cycle 5's deferral is on the record. Cycle 5 deferred the fix because the cycle was already committed and slipping an unrecorded change into the reporting instrument was the exact move that cycle kept refusing. That reasoning was about UNRECORDEDNESS, not about the fix, and it does not survive into a cycle where step 8 has not yet run: rendering the burn-up strip IS step 8's own job, cycle.md step 8 specifies one bar per cycle at height cumulative verified over backlog total, and runs/ is inside the writable half of the hard-rule-5 fence. Deferring a second time would have meant knowingly publishing a flat empty strip for a sixth cycle to the run's only live audience. The fix is recorded here, in the journal, and in KI-36's own resolution field, so it is not unrecorded in any sense. Fixing it also surfaced two sibling hardcodes in the same file and one instrument disagreement between the budget probe and the allocator (KI-37) - which is itself evidence for the D-R8-17 thesis: nobody had read this renderer end to end since it was written, so every confident constant in it had survived untouched.

A SIXTH consecutive cycle of conductor-instrument defects, and the first that CRASHED the gate outright instead of merely misreporting a cell. cycle-008-gate.mjs cell C5 cloned the target repo and then invoked `<clone>/tools/test-line-delta.mjs` to prove the tool is a measurement rather than a constant — but that tool is this cycle's own work and is still UNTRACKED at verification time, and `git clone` carries tracked content only. The clone arrived without the file, node died on MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and the unhandled JSON.parse took the whole gate down before C5 through C13 ever returned a verdict. Ninth distinct root cause in six cycles, and again sharing nothing with the previous eight (five-column parse of a two-column table; .trim() eating a status column; a snapshot used as an invariant; a renderer self-checked against its own hardcoded intent; a first-match regex; a perturbation that never reached its subject; a wrong reporter format; a file assumed into existence — and now a clone assumed to carry an uncommitted file). Handled as every prior instance was: the defect is NAMED in the instrument's own header as defence 7, the fix copies the working-tree tool into the clone and PROVES it arrived (`tool tracked by git? NO (untracked — clone cannot carry it)` prints in the evidence), and every tool invocation now parses defensively and prints its own stderr rather than dying silently. The corrected gate ran 13 cells and the C5 proof it enabled is the strongest failability evidence this run has produced: +46-line file -> delta +125, plus a 298-line file removed -> delta -173 (a NEGATIVE direction the builder never tested), identity control -> 0, and the run's headline +79 printed for none of the three. The RETRO thesis is unchanged and now carries nine instances: one-shot instruments are written once, run once, and reviewed by nobody, while the code they judge gets a builder, a gate, and a converse control.

W-10 PASSES every clause it was dispatched against and the conductor still recorded a defect against the document — the third instance of this ruling shape (cf. D-R8-7, D-R8-8). Gate cell C13 bundled two independent checks and returned one FAIL. Split in cycle-008-gate-c13-addendum.mjs: the scratch-tree half PASSES (no .scratch tree survives), and the commit-count half is a real defect that belongs to no clause W-10 carries. REPORT.md's closing line reads "(13 commits, `912a2a4`..`d899fe0`)"; measured, `git rev-list --count 912a2a4..d899fe0` = 12 because git's A..B excludes A, while `912a2a4^..d899fe0` = 13. 912a2a4 is itself run #8's cycle-0 KICKOFF commit — its parent 20b7ede is run #7's wrap-up and this run's locked baseline — so the run genuinely made 13 commits: the NUMBER is true and the RANGE NOTATION printed beside it selects a different one. W-10's acceptance clause requires the measured test/ before/after, the findings-to-executables ledger, the launchable S-7 escalation and NOT-RUN honesty, and carries no commit-count requirement; the cycle count WRAP_UP does require ("0 through 7 complete, cycle 8 in progress") is correct. Rounding this into a FAIL would discard a verified report over a case its clause never asked for; leaving it unrecorded would be the gate opening itself by silence. Filed as P-3 with the exact measurement and a converse control proving the comparison accepts a correctly-notated claim, so the check that found it cannot be one that fires on everything.

THE RUN'S HEADLINE DELIVERABLE IS WEAKER THAN IT IS PUBLISHED TO BE, and this is the cycle that says so. REPORT.md publishes 'DETECTION FLOOR HOLDS ... 0 detection lost', and tools/detection-floor.mjs's own header claims 'a doctored input MUST turn the run red -- that is the proof this tool is an assertion, not a snapshot'. That specific claim is now FALSIFIED four independent ways, each reproduced by an adversarial verifier against the COMMITTED artifact with no flags (the exact invocation run-all.mjs uses): delete rows from the baseline record and the floor silently shrinks, to zero rows if you like, still HOLDS (RV-2); record an identity control with 7 failing tests and it is still read as GREEN, because only the verdict STRING is consulted (RV-3); record an internally impossible row -- CAUGHT, green suite, no fired guards -- and it is bucketed 'still detected' (RV-4). Worst is RV-1: three of eighteen rows (17%) are exempted as CLAIM-GONE without the suite ever being run for them, on a premise that is FALSE at HEAD. The README matrix table is alive at README.md:198-204 and its three guards are alive and passing at test/readme-matrix-consistency.test.js:125,140,159 -- the conductor ran that file alone, 5/5 green. The anchors died only because commit 4980f3a legitimately moved the table 129/127 -> 128/126 while the mutation strings stayed frozen literals. In a scratch clone the verifier DELETED all three guards, left the table intact, and the tool still printed CLAIM-GONE 'the claim no longer exists', still printed DETECTION FLOOR HOLDS, still exited 0 -- while itself printing 'transcribed guard title not found in the measured tree'. Two fairness notes that belong on the record and do not rescue the claim: the tool's own W8-R1 text DOCUMENTS this failure mode and defers it to tools/guard-inventory.mjs, and the verifier confirmed the substance of the committed verdicts reproduces live (14 same-guard, 1 guard-changed, 3 claim-gone, 0 detection-lost). So the numbers are not fabricated -- what is false is that anything CHECKS them. And the deferral chain fails at its far end too: RV-10 shows guard-inventory's count-floor detector is one-directionally evadable, printing the categorical 'No guard anywhere in test/ (or CI) asserts any floor' while listing the evading guard by title in its own section E. This run RETIRED count-floors on that verdict.

A SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE CYCLE OF CONDUCTOR-INSTRUMENT DEFECTS -- three in this cycle, all three caught, and the catching mechanism is the point. (1) The dependency check printed the label 'no output above = zero-dep holds' directly above three lines of output; the three hits were relative internal requires, so the CONCLUSION was right, but the check's stated pass condition did not match its own output. Re-taken with a real discriminator (a specifier that is neither relative nor node:) plus a converse control that plants lodash and chalk and must find them -- it did. (2) Gate cell C5 for P-3 was offered as a control proving the commit-count check does not pass on any range; it used 20b7ede..d899fe0, which is the SAME RANGE as 912a2a4^..d899fe0 by construction, since 20b7ede IS 912a2a4's parent (verified: rev-parse 912a2a4^ -> 20b7ede). It could never have discriminated. Re-taken with ranges that genuinely differ (15 and 14 against the claimed 13). (3) The first attempt to reproduce RV-11 ran citation-tax with the Bash shell's cwd still at the target from an earlier cd, so the tool resolved correctly and appeared to REFUTE the finding; re-run with an explicit cd to a different repo it reproduced immediately. That third one is the dangerous shape -- an environment artifact that produces a FALSE NEGATIVE, which would have discarded a true finding rather than admitted a false one. Twelve distinct root causes across seven cycles now, still sharing nothing with each other. But note what is different this cycle: the gate was deliberately built WITHOUT a gate script -- direct commands with raw output printed beside each verdict -- precisely because nine of the previous defects were parser bugs sitting between the conductor and the truth. Removing the parser removed that whole class, and all three of this cycle's slips were instead LABEL/CONTROL/ENVIRONMENT errors, each caught by reading the raw output against its own claim. That habit, not care, is what is doing the work -- exactly as D-R8-17 said. The RETRO thesis stands and now carries twelve instances.

RV-9 PASSES every clause it was dispatched against and the conductor still recorded a defect against the tool -- the FOURTH instance of this ruling shape (cf. D-R8-7, D-R8-8, D-R8-21). The clause required 'a minimum-content floor and a rule-identity anchor'; both exist and both work, proven by a discriminator the clause did not ask for: a 136-byte paraphrase OVER the length floor but missing the anchor still fails, so the anchor is doing real work rather than the length test carrying it alone. The residual defect is the anchor's SHAPE. It is a frozen literal, so rewording README's rule clause and the doc's quote TOGETHER -- leaving the doc a byte-identical quote of README, which is exactly the behaviour the tool exists to reward -- exits 1 and prints 'docs/node-support-citation-history.md has diverged', blaming the document that did not diverge. Reproduced by the conductor in a scratch clone (1 occurrence rewritten in README, 2 in the doc, 260-byte quote). Two things make this worth recording rather than burying. First, the attribution direction is wrong in the same way D-R8-7's was, and that is now a recurring shape in this repo's document guards. Second, and worse: RV-1 was a FROZEN-LITERAL defect, and its sibling fix introduced a new frozen literal. The class was not learned, only the instance was patched. Severity is bounded by direction -- RV-1 failed SILENT (exempting 3 of 18 rows from measurement while printing HOLDS), P-4 fails LOUD -- and a loud wrong answer is recoverable in a way a quiet one is not. Filed as P-4 / KI-44 with the exact reproduction and a converse requirement that the three RV-9 cases must all still fail after any fix.

AN EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE CYCLE OF CONDUCTOR-INSTRUMENT DEFECTS -- four in this cycle, all four caught, none by a gate script, because this cycle again had none (cf. D-R8-23). (1) The very first W-6 measurement ran with the Bash shell's cwd still at /opt/swarm from an earlier cd, so it hashed the WRONG REPO and printed an empty protected-path status that was true of SWARM and meaningless about the target. That is the RV-11 defect class -- cwd inheritance producing a confident claim about the wrong repository -- biting the instrument that was checking for it, in the same cycle, and it is the FALSE-NEGATIVE direction, which discards true findings rather than admitting false ones. Re-taken with explicit `git -C`. (2) test_cmd was run against a HAND-EXPANDED file list that both invented three files which do not exist (aphorism/corpus/tags.test.js) and omitted three that do (args/pipe/select.test.js); node --test did not error on the invented ones, so it silently reported 66 tests where the baseline is 128. Caught only because 66 contradicted a known number. Re-taken as the LITERAL test_cmd through a shell so the glob expands: 128/128/0/0. (3) The manifest check used the pattern `.*lock` and matched `journal-block.md` seven times -- a false positive on the word BLOCK. Re-taken with an anchored alternation of real manifest filenames. (4) The dependency classifier omitted the colon from its specifier shape test, so every `node:` builtin failed the test and was dropped BEFORE counting; it printed '0 specifiers scanned' over 29 real imports -- a vacuous NONE that would have read as proof. Caught because the converse control found 2 planted deps while the subject found 0 to look at, which is incoherent. Re-taken with node:/relative/foreign bucketed separately: 29 = 29 + 0 + 0. THIRTEEN through SIXTEEN distinct root causes across eight cycles, still sharing nothing with each other. The constant is unchanged and now has sixteen instances: one-shot instruments are written once, run once, and reviewed by nobody, while the code they judge gets a builder, a gate and a converse control. But note what caught all four: a number that contradicted a known baseline, a control that disagreed with its own subject, and raw output printed beside its own label. Not care -- structure. Every one of these was caught by the SAME habit D-R8-17 named: print the evidence next to the claim and read whether they agree. That habit is the run's primary RETRO candidate and it is now the only thing standing between this conductor and a false report.

BACKLOG ID COLLISION, found at orient and repaired before dispatch. Cycle 10 filed its follow-up item as W-14 -- an id already held by a DONE cycle-5 item -- so backlog.json carried two live entries under one key, and a lookup by id returned whichever came first (the done one). Nothing downstream had consumed the bad id yet, because the item was filed at the end of cycle 10 and this is the first cycle to read it. Renamed to W-15, the collision recorded in the item's own notes, and the whole backlog re-scanned: zero duplicate ids remain across 51 items. The generalisable point is that the id is the ONLY handle the pipeline has on an item -- state.json, the journal, the dashboard and the gate all address items by id -- so a duplicate is not cosmetic; it silently redirects a verdict onto the wrong row. Cheap to detect (one pass over the array) and it was never checked. Cycle 10's own hygiene pass at cycle % 5 == 0 reported 'no duplicates' one cycle before creating this one, which is honest -- the duplicate did not exist yet -- but it means the check ran at the one moment it could not catch this.

A CATEGORICAL NEGATIVE FROM A STATIC SCAN MUST BE BOUNDED BY ITS SEARCH -- ruled at RV-10, and the ruling is broader than the item. guard-inventory printed 'VERDICT: ABSENT. No guard anywhere in test/ (or CI) asserts any floor', a universal claim over all possible code, on the strength of two regexes. It was evadable in one direction: the same working floor guard written '120 < n' rather than 'n > 120' produced NONE/NONE/ABSENT while section E listed that very guard by title, three lines earlier. This run RETIRED count-floor guards on the strength of that verdict, so the sentence was load-bearing. The clause offered two routes (widen the detectors OR bound the sentence) and the builder took both, correctly: widening alone leaves a universal claim no static scan can underwrite at any width, and bounding alone leaves a detector blind to the commoner operand order. What makes the fix structural rather than cosmetic is that section G now prints its probe list by iterating the SAME FLOOR_PROBES table the scan iterates, so the published description of the search cannot drift from the search.
